subject: Edge traffic evacuation advisory — temporary fallback steps and post-incident follow-up
content:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmetech.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2029 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: Immediate edge traffic evacuation — temporary fallback steps

Samir —

We wanted to alert you immediately: between 07:45 and 08:05 PST we observed a cascading connectivity degradation affecting a subset of our US-east edge PoPs and two EU peering points. This has resulted in elevated 5xx error rates and timeouts for a fraction of requests routed through those locations.

What we have done so far
- Identified the impacted PoPs and isolated the affected peering sessions.
- Shifted control-plane routing to healthy POPs and enabled automated fallbacks to the nearest healthy region.
- Implemented temporary capacity shedding on low-priority background requests to preserve serving for foreground traffic.

Immediate action for AcmeTech
- If you have a strict zone affinity policy, you can opt in to our emergency fallback to route requests to our us-west or eu-central clusters. This does not require DNS changes; we will push a routing policy on your account unless you explicitly decline.
- If you prefer to control the switch from your side, apply the attached fallback checklist — key steps are TTL reduction for your DNS and a 60-minute window to verify.

Attachments: evacuation-fallback-checklist.pdf (see section 2 for opt-in commands)

Please reply with which option you prefer (Redwood-managed fallback OR customer-managed switch). If we don’t hear back in 30 minutes we will enable the Redwood-managed fallback to avoid further customer impact.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you posted with more technical detail and a post-incident summary once the full investigation completes.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmetech.com>

Cc: support@acmetech.com
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2029 09:02:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: Immediate edge traffic evacuation — temporary fallback steps

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads up. We just started seeing 502/504 spikes around 07:50 and our metrics show increased retries. We’d prefer Redwood-managed fallback for speed — our app has brittle DNS automation right now. Can you confirm:
- Will sessions be sticky to the fallback region (we need session affinity for search indices)?
- Any expected latency increase to our primary workflows if routed to eu-central vs us-west?

If you need us to reduce DNS TTL we can do it, but don’t wait on us; please proceed if that’s the safer path.

— Samir
Senior Infrastructure Lead
AcmeTech

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmetech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2029 12:30:45 -0800
Subject: RE: Notice: Immediate edge traffic evacuation — temporary fallback steps

Hi Samir —

Short answers first:
- Stickiness: the Redwood-managed fallback preserves session affinity by routing requests through a per-customer session selector. For JWT/session-cookie workloads we maintain affinity for a 15-minute sliding window; for long-lived websockets we will not forcibly tear sessions (we will only prevent new connections to the unhealthy POPs).
- Latency: us-west is the lower-latency fallback for your US users (typical +20–60ms). eu-central will add +120–180ms for US origin traffic; we prefer us-west unless your regulatory policy requires EU-only routing.

Technical detail (what we did and how to opt out)
- We failed over three affected US-east PoPs and bounded the peering flap with BGP dampening; healthy PoPs in us-west and eu-central accepted shifted traffic.
- For Redwood-managed fallback we modified your account routing policy: {account-routing: emergency-fallback: us-west>eu-central}. This will remain in place until the control-plane rollback (targeted) occurs.
- To opt out and perform a customer-managed switch: see commands in attached edge-reroute-commands.txt. Key steps: reduce DNS TTL to 60s, update CNAME to the secondary endpoint, monitor error-rate.

Attachments: edge-reroute-commands.txt (contains curl examples, API flags and exact policy payloads)

We’re also opening a follow-up SOC/ops ticket to capture packet captures and peering logs. I’ll attach the logs in the post-incident bundle.

Let me know if you want us to keep the session-affinity window longer for your account (we can extend to 30 minutes but it may increase token duplication on retries).

-David
David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmetech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2029 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident notes: edge peering disruption (Nov 30) and next steps

Samir —

Thanks again for the quick coordination earlier today and for confirming Redwood-managed fallback. Here is a concise post-incident summary and immediate next steps we have for AcmeTech.

What happened
- Root cause (preliminary): transient peering flaps at two upstream exchange points caused a control-plane regression in our US-east edge scheduler. This produced partial packet loss and elevated downstream 5xx rates for some customer routes.
- Impact windows: 07:45–09:10 PST (most affected), with residual elevated retries until 11:20 PST for a small percentage of sessions.

Customer-specific actions taken
- We enabled Redwood-managed fallback to us-west for AcmeTech at 08:20 PST.
- Session affinity behavior preserved per David’s note; we extended affinity to 25 minutes for your account at your request.
- We collected peering logs and selected packet captures; attaching sanitized logs in the postmortem bundle.

What we’re doing next (short and medium term)
- Short term: complete packet capture analysis and a configuration audit for the edge scheduler; ETA 72 hours.
- Medium term: deploy improved BGP dampening thresholds and add an automated health-check quorum for peering re-acceptance; ETA 3–4 weeks.

Credits and verification
- Per our SLA we will evaluate the outage window and propose a credits package if the event meets the SLA breach criteria. We’ll follow up with a formal credit offer in 5 business days.
- Please verify your error-rate graph in the attached postmortem-summary-20291130.md and confirm if you see residual issues on your side.

Attachments: postmortem-summary-20291130.md, sanitized-peering-logs.tar.gz (link provided in the incident ticket)

If you’d like an engineering sync, we can schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the packet captures and remediation timeline.

Appreciate your patience — we know any disruption is costly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
